final_narrative:
The enrichment analysis identifies **Eicosanoid Synthesis (Wikipathways WP167)** as the dominant affected pathway, with an FDR of 0.0 and an extraordinary fold-enrichment of 1250.9 — reflecting that 5 of the 8 input metabolites (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2) all map to this 27-compound pathway against a background of over 54,000 compounds. This is the single most coherent biological signal in the dataset.

**Key driver compounds** are **arachidonic acid (C00219)** and **leukotriene A4 (C00909)**, both confirmed members of Eicosanoid Synthesis (Wikipathways WP167). KEGG graph traversal confirms that arachidonic acid lies upstream of leukotriene A4, connected via a two-step reaction (arachidonic acid → 5-HPETE → leukotriene A4). Arachidonic acid is also the precursor of 15-HETE via the 15-HPETE intermediate, establishing a forward biosynthetic route through the 15-lipoxygenase arm. Together these compounds form a coherent cascade reflecting activation of the 5- and 15-lipoxygenase arms of the arachidonic acid cascade. 15-Deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2, a cyclopentenone prostaglandin, is also part of this network and maps to the same pathway.

**Biological significance**: Eicosanoids are potent lipid mediators governing inflammation, pain, and immune cell trafficking. Coordinated elevation of arachidonic acid alongside its lipoxygenase products (5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4) and a cyclopentenone prostaglandin strongly implicates an active inflammatory or pro-resolving response in the treatment condition. Acetylcysteine is not among the five input metabolites mapped to Eicosanoid Synthesis (Wikipathways WP167). Dopamine and fructose-1-phosphate are also not among the five metabolites mapped to Eicosanoid Synthesis (Wikipathways WP167). In summary, the data point to robust activation of the arachidonic acid–eicosanoid axis, with arachidonic acid as the upstream substrate driving the observed accumulation of downstream lipoxygenase products.

**Limitations**: Acetylcysteine, dopamine, and fructose-1-phosphate do not appear among the metabolites mapped to the enriched Eicosanoid Synthesis (Wikipathways WP167), and no other pathway reached significance in the RaMP analysis, leaving the relevance of these three metabolites to the study uncharacterised in the pathway context.
